questions.q: What is the Dollar Challenge designed to help you get past?
a: The fear of starting a business
The habit of overspending on ads
The urge to copy competitors
The difficulty of hiring staff
questions.why: Lesson 1 says asking someone for a dollar forces you out of your comfort zone and makes you accountable.

questions.q: What is the point of the Coffee Challenge?
a: To practice asking and hearing no without fear
To learn how coffee shops set their prices
To find a cheaper place to work each day
To test whether discounts raise sales
questions.why: Lesson 1 says most people will be rejected, and the lesson is that everything will be fine.

questions.q: Which source does the summary call the best place to find a business idea?
a: A problem you run into yourself
A bestseller you could complement
A marketplace full of eager buyers
A popular search suggestion
questions.why: Lesson 2 lists four sources and calls solving your own problem the king of them.

questions.q: What does the summary say customers actually care about?
a: Whether your idea solves a problem they have
How original and clever your concept is
How much funding you have raised so far
Whether your brand looks professional
questions.why: Lesson 2 says customers do not care about your ideas, only about whether you can solve their problems.

questions.q: What counts as validating a business idea in the summary?
a: Getting three people to pay within 48 hours
Getting a hundred people to join a waitlist
Receiving positive feedback from friends
Selling advertising on a simple landing page
questions.why: Lesson 3 calls this the Golden Rule of Validation and says to move on if it fails.
